scope: Agent audit findings 1-5; sandbox deferred by user
worktree: Existing concurrent edits preserved; no commit, push, release, or running-server restart

repairs.cause: Multiple callers consumed one transport queue; an inline notification could reenter request handling and consume another request's reply.
repairs.invariant: One receiver routes replies to request-id waiters. Notifications execute separately. Shutdown wakes pending calls; cancellation is best effort.
repairs.ab: Legal reversed replies: old path loses both replies; repaired path returns A to A and B to B. Notification during an active call: old path times out; repaired path completes.

repairs.cause: Timeout/cancellation discarded the executing action identity and side-effect class. MCP timeouts were flattened into terminal generic errors.
repairs.invariant: An unconfirmed side effect returns unknown, nonretryable, incomplete, and retains its action id. Unresolved identical operations are not repeated just because the model generates a new tool-call id.
repairs.ab: Outer timeout: error/retryable/no action id becomes unknown/nonretryable/retained action id. Inner timeout plus new tool-call id: two delayed external effects become one effect and one blocked repeat.
repairs.boundary: A timeout does not prove remote cancellation. The operation hash only protects identical unresolved arguments within the journal's session; it is not universal business-level exactly-once execution. Confirmed successful identical operations remain repeatable. Persistent protection requires session identity and ActionJournal; XEYO_ACTION_JOURNAL=0 explicitly disables it. Unknown actions require reconciliation before that identical operation can execute again.

repairs.cause: Each child and follow-up cycle created an independent spending tracker with no parent money/token gate.
repairs.invariant: Root, child, and follow-up usage settles into the same task ledger. Per-agent usage remains separate. Every model retry rechecks the shared limit.
repairs.ab: Parent 0.1 USD plus child/follow-up 0.4 USD reaches the shared 0.5 USD gate. A real offline query loop stops after child spending instead of issuing the next parent model request; tool-call/result pairing remains valid.
repairs.boundary: Admission uses settled reported usage. Already in-flight provider requests can overshoot. Unpriced usage remains unknown. This is not a prepaid hard spending cap or a billing guarantee.

repairs.cause: Interrupt and steer targeted only a session, so a delayed request intended for turn A could act on turn B.
repairs.invariant: Updated GUI, TUI, and attached CLI capture the observed turn id. Backend comparison and action share lifecycle locking; interrupt additionally validates the pool lease. Stale requests return 409 before changing queue/control state.
repairs.ab: A stop request carrying A while B is active changes from stopping B to 409 without stopping or pausing B. Stale steer cannot enqueue a message. Queue submissions retain the active GUI turn identity.
repairs.boundary: Requests omitting expected_turn_id retain the legacy session-wide API. A valid admitted steer retains the existing durable fallback-to-inbox contract if no further sampling boundary occurs.

repairs.cause: The child wrapper retained hardcoded provider/model defaults and omitted usage fields when adapting the runner result.
repairs.invariant: Identity comes from the actual model client. Child clients own their per-call observation fields. Adapter, progress event, metadata, and GUI preserve token count, nullable cost, partial-cost flag, and stop reason.
repairs.ab: An Anthropic client keeps its actual identity instead of DeepSeek defaults. 1234 tokens, 1.25 CNY, and partial=true survive adaptation instead of becoming zero, null, and absent.
